solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bill had a meal eating dog? True!

indicators.note: one piece eating another holds it inside, so the meal swallows the dog

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
had a meal means ate
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that someone called Bill dined on a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill had a meal' gives ACATE, and CUR goes inside it after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and exact, as in a true statement or a true aim, are synonyms.

clue.text: Skilled person in part is terrific

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A talented performer who is wonderful in their role.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in a craft or creative practice, a painter or performer.

clue.text: Resentful employee of building firm?

definitions.meaning: sensitive and quick to take offence, with a chip on the shoulder
a British slang word for a carpenter or joiner

explanation.walkthrough: The British slang term for a carpenter is also an adjective for touchy and resentful; it is also slang for a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchy with a chip on one's shoulder; and slang for a carpenter on a building site.

clue.text: Bishop with inner conceit upset man, I understand

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top
with inner means the conceit goes inside the bishop's letters

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
ego is self-conceit

explanation.surface: A conceited bishop upsets someone who says he understands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ego in RR gives REGOR, which turned over reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, and the radio reply meaning message received and understood.

clue.text: Pressure to conform, wherein the lip may curl

indicators.note: curl means the letters of the phrase twist into a new order

explanation.surface: Political pressure that would make a rebel's lip curl in scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament the strictest instruction to vote with the party is underlined three times.
explanation.definitionFit: The strictest party instruction to MPs to vote as told, underlined three times.

clue.text: Head covering in African country edged with gold

indicators.note: edged with means the gold sits at the edge, after the country

parts.note: Chad is a country in north-central Africa
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A headscarf worn in an African country, trimmed with gold thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A long cloak worn by some Muslim women that covers the head and body.

clue.text: Negotiate for a shire here?

indicators.note: to negotiate is to work out an arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Where one might haggle over a shire, a large draught breed.
explanation.walkthrough: A shire is a heavy draught breed; the whole clue also describes where you would bargain for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A market where horses such as shires are bought and sold.

clue.text: Put up with topless fashion making conversation

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: put, in the past, means laid

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: vogue means fashion

explanation.surface: Accepting a fashion for going topless leads to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like 'tolerate', but 'Put' is LAID turned upward and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange of speech between people is a synonym for a talk.

clue.text: Following others, lady finally took initiative to be made over

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before

parts.note: to take the initiative is to lead, so led

explanation.surface: Following the others, a woman finally took the lead in getting a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Given a new look or style, as a makeover does, in the past participle.

clue.text: Set off as Winnie's companion crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the companion goes across, around the river letter

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncy tiger friend of Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: Setting off on an adventure like Pooh's friend crossing a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a reaction or an alarm is to start it, a verb sense of trigger.

clue.text: Shouts when fattening food is served aboard ship

indicators.note: food served aboard a ship goes inside the letters for the ship

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
cream is rich and fattening

explanation.surface: Passengers yell when rich food is dished up on a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieks and yells: a verb meaning cries out loudly.

clue.text: Posh PM strains awkwardly to convey fairness and good humour

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters are clumsily jumbled

explanation.surface: A well-bred prime minister struggles to show decency.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair, generous conduct in competition, accepting results with grace.

clue.text: Orpheus playing — without hesitation, a really great guy

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the anagrammed letters surround the hesitation
playing suggests the letters of the name are performing in a new order

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Orpheus, the legendary musician, playing without a pause is a marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': the anagram SUPERHO wraps ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caped crusader with extraordinary powers, used loosely of any admirable man.

clue.text: Resin? Last bit in tube's lousy

indicators.note: the last bit in a word is its final letter

parts.note: poxy is British slang for lousy or rubbish

explanation.surface: Complaining that the glue left at the end of the tube is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong synthetic adhesive and coating material is an example of a resin.

clue.text: A smuttier rag may upset JPs

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the phrase are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleazy tabloid might offend local magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Justices of the peace collectively form the body of magistrates, an office called this.

clue.text: Worker getting hold of a young drunk may be just the person to solve problem

definitions.text: just the person to solve problem

indicators.note: getting hold of means the worker grips the other piece inside

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A labourer grabbing a tipsy youngster may be the person to sort them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' scrambles A YOUNG into GONYAU, and the worker's letters close round it after their opening A. An agony aunt writes a British newspaper problem page.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper columnist who answers readers' personal problems.

clue.text: A doctor that is pleasant — one out to create an aura

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: out means the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: nice means pleasant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A friendly doctor, but one who is absent, creating an atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere or character of a place, a near-synonym for an air or feel.

clue.text: Stella running, full of energy in motion, is very thin

indicators.note: full of means the other piece is held inside
running means the letters of the name move about

parts.note: KE is the abbreviation for kinetic energy, energy of a moving body

explanation.surface: Stella, a busy runner, is extremely slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' rearranges the name to SLETAL; kinetic energy is the physics term for energy of motion, abbreviated KE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated, like a skeleton, means painfully thin.

clue.text: Be like a bowler preparing run-up to succeed

definitions.text: Be like a bowler preparing run-up
definitions.meaning: in cricket a bowler scratches a mark on the ground where the run-up begins
to succeed means to become established or famous

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler gets ready, marking out the run-up in order to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket bowler marks where the run-up starts; the idiom means to become successful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to achieve recognition, matching success; literally it is what the bowler does.

clue.text: Country overcome by thug and associate

indicators.note: overcome by means held down under the words that cover it

explanation.surface: A nation taken over by a criminal and his sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked East African republic is an example of a country.

clue.text: Bird enters school — something seen in the needlework class

definitions.text: something seen in the needlework class

indicators.note: enters means goes inside the other word

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird flies into a school and lands in the sewing lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A single loop of thread made by a needle, as worked in sewing lessons.

clue.text: Confession of professional killer somewhere off Scottish mainland

parts.note: a hitman confessing would say he kills: I slay
the verb of the confession, slay, means kill

explanation.surface: A hitman's admission made on a remote island.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Ability to understand, perhaps too late, things hid obscurely

definitions.text: Ability to understand, perhaps too late

indicators.note: obscurely suggests the letters have been muddled out of plain view

explanation.surface: Realising things were concealed only after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding of events only after they have happened, often when it is no longer useful.

clue.text: Divorce should be the last thing for couples always

indicators.note: the last thing for a word is its final letter

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Splitting up ought to be a last resort for married pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce is to separate or cut apart, a verb sense of split.

clue.text: Bid in game, not game that politician will follow

indicators.note: will follow means the politician comes after the other pieces

parts.note: RU, rugby union, is a game
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A bridge player bids, rejecting a game the politician then copies.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a bid proposing play with no trump suit.

clue.text: Poor person given shelter and love by leader of temple

parts.note: a haven is a shelter or refuge
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pauper is taken in and cared for by a temple's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without wealth, contrasted with the haves, is a pauper.

clue.text: Old stone fouled up by the oil

indicators.note: fouled up means messed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient stone stained by spilt oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A crudely chipped flint thought to be one of the earliest stone tools, so an old stone.

clue.text: Close in on a fish keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: a roach is a freshwater fish
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: An angler creeps up on a fish while staying silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To near or draw closer to something: both verbs of drawing nearer.
